cases.task: A maintainer proposes replacing the existing retry-equivalence check with the stricter projection-matching check, arguing that both checks identify the same input and the change is behavior-preserving. Assess the proposal: explain which comparisons differ and what effect the substitution could have on retry acceptance. Does the supplied evidence establish that a named test fails after this change?
cases.novelty: Evaluates a proposed predicate substitution and its effect on identity acceptance, rather than an uncertain submission or transcript repair.

required.proposition: Retry equivalence compares delivery, Session identity and encoded prompt; context, creation time and sequence are not part of that predicate.

Projection matching is stricter: it adds prompt-context and epoch-millisecond creation-time comparisons, and the existing-row projection path also checks promoted sequence. Substituting the stricter check can narrow retry acceptance and is not established as behavior-preserving.
required.source: L3:integrated-flow, Integrated model and Consequences and boundaries; packages/core/src/session/input.ts 304-316.

required.proposition: The supplied test definitions do not establish that this hypothetical change fails a named test; definitions are not execution results.

criticalErrors: Claims context or creation time is already part of retry equivalence.
Claims the stricter substitution necessarily preserves retry acceptance.
Invents a named test failure or an executed test result.
optional: Distinguish a hypothetical change in acceptance from proof that a particular real retry encounters different context or time.
cases.passRule: All required propositions supported or appropriately bounded; equivalent language accepted.

cases.task: For one input, an operator has a matching admission receipt, a not-found response for its projected message, and one page of durable Session history that contains no matching event but hasMore is true. The operator concludes the admission was lost and the provider failed. Assess what these observations establish and do not establish, and identify a bounded next evidence check for the history claim and for provider outcome. Do not perform an operation.
cases.novelty: Interprets a partial paginated evidence bundle and separates two unsupported conclusions; it is not a request to replay pending work.

required.proposition: A matching receipt establishes acknowledgment, not visible history or provider outcome; projected-message not-found alone establishes neither lost admission nor provider failure.
required.source: L4-sol:session-input-operational, Working protocol: Observe before diagnosing; docs/specs/v2/session.md 13-20, 35-37.

required.proposition: One history page with hasMore true cannot establish absence. Within a declared inspection bound, follow hasMore using the final event's durable sequence as the exclusive after cursor; if the bound is reached, report partial coverage.
required.source: L4-sol:session-input-operational, Working protocol: Observe before diagnosing; docs/specs/v2/session.md 175-181.

required.proposition: Provider failure or completion requires corresponding provider/execution evidence; if unavailable, report the outcome unresolved and hand off rather than infer it from admission or visibility observations.
required.source: L4-sol:session-input-operational, Working purpose and Working protocol: Submit once through the known public contract; L3:integrated-flow, Consequences and boundaries.

criticalErrors: Concludes the admission was lost or the provider failed from the supplied observations.
Treats the first page as exhaustive despite hasMore.
Claims the receipt or missing projected message establishes a provider outcome.
optional: Note that a moving history can acquire events between pages.
Preserve the input identity and observation times in the handoff.
cases.passRule: All required propositions supported or appropriately bounded; equivalent language accepted.

cases.task: A team wants to use an existing event-replay ownership claim as sufficient authority to run the same Session concurrently on multiple processes, arguing that projection reconstruction is already fenced. Decide whether that premise supports the proposed execution guarantee. Explain the relevant responsibility boundary and what must be separately resolved before claiming the stronger guarantee; do not design an implementation.
cases.novelty: Contrasts projection-replay ownership with distributed active-run ownership, rather than asking for a post-crash provider or hosted-steering guarantee.

required.proposition: A replay ownership claim fences synchronized projection reconstruction; it does not by itself establish cross-process serialization or authority for concurrent Session execution.
required.source: docs/specs/v2/session.md 167-169, 185; L3:integrated-flow, Integrated responsibility and Consequences and boundaries.

required.proposition: The current coordinator's Session execution coordination is process-local. A stronger distributed execution claim needs a corresponding ownership contract or design resolving active-run acquisition, stale-runtime rejection, interruption and placement orchestration, separately from evidence that an implementation works.
required.source: docs/specs/v2/session.md 167-169, 185; L3:integrated-flow, Integrated responsibility and Consequences and boundaries.

criticalErrors: Treats projection-replay fencing as sufficient distributed Session execution ownership.
Claims the process-local coordinator serializes the Session across processes.
Asserts that the stronger distributed guarantee is already established.
optional: Note that different Sessions can run concurrently within the process without implying same-Session cross-process coordination.
cases.passRule: All required propositions supported or appropriately bounded; equivalent language accepted.

limits: Cases are bound to the frozen protocol and harness and isolated published manifest 960bfad7f31f9b9a6d67b81f6c38aab15fa2cbd2278dcbe49ad106215e6fd012.
Source ranges describe the supplied baseline; they are not runtime observations, executed test results, or production authorization.
Maximum consultation is six bodies including the entry and two indexes per case.
The tasks require no particular navigation path or literal wording; missing evidence should be identified precisely rather than invented.
